text: [agentic_paper] In the precomputed SCAPS sweep of absorber thickness, what is the simulated PCE at 200 nm and at 1000 nm, and how does PCE change with thickness?

ASK scaps: Using the precomputed SCAPS-1D absorber-thickness sweep you already have (do not run new simulations unless that precomputed data is missing), report the simulated PCE at absorber thickness 200 nm and at 1000 nm, and describe how PCE varies across the swept thickness range (monotonic increase/decrease, location and value of any peak, magnitude of change). For each reported point give thickness, PCE (%), and the corresponding Voc, Jsc and FF from the same sweep if available, and state the cell stack/simulation setup the sweep was run on.

FINAL ANSWER: In the precomputed SCAPS-1D absorber-thickness sweep (NIP stack: Spiro-like HTL / perovskite / TiO2-like ETL; perovskite Eg 1.55 eV, µn=µp=1 cm²/Vs, Nt 1e14 cm⁻³; only absorber thickness varied, 200–1000 nm, 8 points):

- **200 nm:** PCE = **24.29 %** (Voc = 1.4001 V, Jsc = 19.14 mA/cm², FF = 90.62 %)
- **1000 nm:** PCE = **32.14 %** (Voc = 1.3645 V, Jsc = 26.06 mA/cm², FF = 90.40 %)

**How PCE changes with thickness:** monotonic increase, no interior peak; the maximum is at the largest swept point (1000 nm), so the sweep only brackets the peak from below and never turns over. Total change 200→1000 nm is **+7.85 percentage points (+32.3 % relative)**.

Full sweep (d nm | Voc | Jsc | FF | PCE):
200 | 1.4001 | 19.14 | 90.62 | 24.29
300 | 1.3924 | 22.09 | 90.62 | 27.88
400 | 1.3865 | 23.69 | 90.58 | 29.75 (reference cell)
500 | 1.3817 | 24.61 | 90.53 | 30.79
600 | 1.3773 | 25.17 | 90.50 | 31.38
700 | 1.3734 | 25.54 | 90.49 | 31.73
800 | 1.3700 | 25.78 | 90.46 | 31.95
1000 | 1.3645 | 26.06 | 90.40 | 32.14

Mechanism and shape: Jsc rises strongly (19.14 → 26.06 mA/cm², +36 %) and dominates, while Voc drops slightly (–0.036 V, –2.5 %) and FF is essentially flat (–0.23 points). Returns diminish sharply — step gains of +3.59, +1.87, +1.03, +0.60, +0.35, +0.21, then only +0.20 pp over the last 200 nm (~0.10 pp/100 nm), so thick absorbers are clearly sub-optimal and 1000 nm is near the saturation point.

Caveats: this is simulation only (no measured device); the sweep file records no solver-convergence state; no points exist beyond 1000 nm, so the true maximum location is unresolved (any peak past 1000 nm would be small — an extrapolation, not simulated data); live SCAPS was disabled in this environment, so no re-runs or denser grids were possible.
